summary.intent: Debug two related CipherBox FUSE bugs on macOS: (1) folder rename requiring elevated permissions and still failing, and (2) web UI folder rename + sync creating a duplicate folder instead of renaming the existing one.
summary.outcome: Both bugs were diagnosed and fixed in the Rust FUSE crate, unit tests and e2e tests were added, all changes were committed to a feature branch, and three unresolved debug sessions were archived to the resolved folder.

repo: macOS FUSE-T uses an SMB backend that performs its own UID-based permission checks against getattr results — when the SMB client UID doesn't match the FUSE-reported owner, write ops (including rename) are denied regardless of FUSE-level logic.
CipherBox uses encryption as the real access control, so FUSE directory permissions should be 0o777 and file permissions 0o666 rather than restrictive Unix defaults.
populate_folder() in inode.rs previously matched children by display name only; stable IPNS names are the correct identity key for detecting renames vs. new folders.
Debug sessions are tracked as markdown files in .planning/debug/*.md with a status field and archived to .planning/debug/resolved/ when complete.
The GSD workflow uses a gsd-debugger subagent type (not general-purpose) with session state persisted in .planning/debug/{slug}.md to enable continuation across context boundaries.
SDK folder mutation scripts live in packages/sdk-core/scripts/*.mjs and use renameInFolder() from packages/sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts — this is the same code path as the web UI.
E2e desktop tests split into test-fuse-operations.sh/.ps1 (FUSE layer) and test-cross-client-sync.sh (sync reconciliation); both need updating when adding new FUSE capabilities.
Pre-commit hooks enforce markdownlint and prettier; these must pass before a commit lands.

code.finding: populate_folder() needed a secondary lookup map keyed by ipns_name so renames (same IPNS identity, new display name) are detected and the old inode reused rather than a duplicate allocated. Two unit tests cover merge_only=true and merge_only=false paths.
Directory permissions changed from 0o755 to 0o777, file permissions from 0o644 to 0o666, to prevent macOS FUSE-T's SMB layer from blocking writes/renames on UID mismatch.
renameInFolder() is the authoritative rename API used by the web UI; e2e sync tests should call this via the new rename-folder.mjs script to faithfully simulate web-initiated renames.
Tests 6b (directory rename via mv) and 6c (cross-directory file move) added to cover FUSE permission fix; test 8 cleanup updated to include new folder names.
Tests 6 and 7 added: SDK-initiated folder rename followed by FUSE-side polling (up to 120s) to verify renamed folder appears and old folder disappears without duplicates.
New script created to authenticate, load vault metadata, call renameInFolder(), and republish — mirrors the web UI rename flow for use in e2e sync tests.

workflow: Spawning a dedicated gsd-debugger subagent isolates investigation context (file reads, hypothesis cycles) from the main orchestrator context, keeping the conversation lean.
Parallel agent spawning (FUSE fix agent + sync fix agent simultaneously) is effective when the two bugs share a file but have independent root causes.
Verification step after agent completion is essential — agents summarize what they intended to do, not necessarily what they did; always read the actual diff.
Unit tests alone are insufficient for FUSE runtime behavior on macOS; e2e desktop tests covering both the FUSE layer and the sync reconciliation path are required for confidence.

friction: Initial attempt launched generic research agents before the GSD debug workflow was invoked; the user had to interrupt and redirect to the correct gsd-debugger subagent pattern.

The final commit moving debug files to the resolved folder did not complete cleanly — the transcript shows files still appearing as modified after the commit bash command, suggesting the mv + stage + commit sequence had an issue.
Verifying the run_rename_folder helper required an extra read step because the agent's summary didn't confirm whether the helper was inserted in the right location.
open_items: Bug 1 (FUSE permission fix) has no automated test coverage — the 0o755→0o777 change can only be validated by manually mounting the filesystem on macOS and attempting a rename without elevation.
Linux and Windows FUSE rename behavior is untested; the permission fix may behave differently on those platforms.

The fuse-stale-file-after-web-edit and google-oauth-tauri-redirect debug sessions were marked resolved and archived but the transcript gives no indication their underlying fixes were implemented — worth confirming those are actually resolved.
